newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto orders firms to give to poor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto orders firms to give to poor.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto has ordered individuals and companies with annual after-tax profits of over 100 million rupiah ($42,000) to give two percent of their earnings to the poor.
"Individuals and companies have to give two percent of their after-tax profit to poor families in one tax year," Suharto said in a decree released on Friday.
The decree, dated December 4 and effective in the 1996 tax year, was released by the State Secretariat.
Suharto in September asked Indonesia's wealthy why they had ignored a government appeal to donate two percent of their profits to alleviate poverty.
It was not immediately clear how the decree would be enforced.

The 1995 appeal for donations to the government's poverty alleviation programme was issued in the form of a presidential decree and addressed to private companies and individuals with an after-tax income of more than 100 million rupiah a year.
The December 4 order changed the words in section two of the 1995 decree to say companies and individuals "must give" to the poor, instead of "can help" the poor.
About 80 percent of Indonesia's nearly 200 million people are Moslems, who are expected under their faith to donate part of their income to charity.
